# Nirium Watch

> Live settlement checks for x402 APIs on Stellar testnet. A 402 is a promise; a settled transaction is proof. Built at HackMeridian 2026 (remote, Genesis track, not prize-eligible).

Nirium Watch pays each monitored x402 endpoint the way an AI agent would, with our own testnet key, then reads the transaction back from Stellar RPC (`getTransaction`) and confirms a SAC transfer of the required amount reached the required `payTo`. Each check round is signed with an ed25519 monitor key and pinned to IPFS as one receipt (`nirium-audit-v1` record format). On a state change (settled to failing, or back), it sends an HMAC-signed alert to Pullcord.

Facilitators checked: OpenZeppelin (through our own Nirium testnet agent), Rail402 (hosted demo + Bazaar discovery), AgentSmith (our own seller on their public testnet facilitator). Rumble Fish, also funded in SCF #45, is not checked yet: on 26-oct-2026 its public repo had no testnet facilitator to call.

## Links

- [Live status page](https://nirium-watch.vercel.app/): per-endpoint status, settled transactions, receipts, alerts
- [Source code](https://github.com/Eras256/nirium-watch): MIT, TypeScript
- [README](https://github.com/Eras256/nirium-watch/blob/main/README.md): architecture, setup, prior work disclosure, honest limits
- [Raw check history](https://github.com/Eras256/nirium-watch/blob/main/data/history.json): every check, with tx hash and receipt CID

## Honest limits

- Testnet only. All payments come from our own team key: this is not adoption or external traffic.
- No partnerships with OpenZeppelin, Rail402, AgentSmith or Rumble Fish; we only call public testnet endpoints.
- Nirium (x402 client, receipt format, testnet agent) and Pullcord (alert service) are the team's own earlier projects, disclosed. Everything in the repo was written during HackMeridian.
- One failed check is not proof a facilitator is down; the page shows history, not verdicts.
